kwargs.profile_path: the profile directory being audited: profile['path'] in audit_surface._sweep (the same value write_settings and skill_hygiene receive). The module is self-contained: it reads no config.yaml key and opens no credential file, so this is the only argument the caller passes.
kwargs.huge_file_threshold_bytes: optional, do not pass (default HUGE_FILE_THRESHOLD_BYTES = 50 MiB)
kwargs.clock: optional, do not pass (default time.monotonic; tests inject it)

consequences.home_workdirs.could_not_verify: Home workdir inspection hit a safety cap or could not read part of the home; incomplete traversal is reported as could_not_verify rather than clean.
consequences.home_workdirs.huge_files: Files other than Hermes's own databases are at or above the single-file size threshold; this records size and file type only and does not show who wrote them or whether they are still needed.
consequences.home_workdirs.nested_hermes_homes: Directories below the home root, outside named profiles, hold config.yaml together with a Hermes home marker name; this counts them by file name only and does not show how they were made or whether Hermes uses them.
consequences.home_workdirs.oversized_hermes_folders: Folders that Hermes creates (plans, tools, venvs) hold more than the threshold in files that are not the kind Hermes writes there; this measures file names and sizes only and does not show who wrote them or whether they are still needed.
consequences.home_workdirs.working_trees_in_home: Virtual environments, copied source trees, dependency folders, repositories or archives beside an extracted copy were found by marker names outside Hermes's own dependency folders; this counts them and their bytes and does not show whether anything still uses them.
consequences.home_workdirs.work_folders_in_home: Top-level folders whose names the Hermes source never creates hold more than the size or share threshold of this home's bytes; this is a measurement of names, sizes and file counts and does not show who created them or whether they are still needed.

free_strings.what: absolute path of an existing item inside the audited home, under the resolved home (os.path.realpath): home_workdirs.not_hermes_folders[].path (<profile>/<top-level name>), home_workdirs.huge_files[].path (the file, or its second-level folder when deeper: never more than two components below the home), home_workdirs.hermes_databases.files[].path (<profile>/[profiles/<name>/]<Hermes database file>), and each finding's source_paths[].path (the home, <profile>/<top-level name> for the first 10 shown not-Hermes folders, <profile>/plans|tools|venvs). When the name is undecodable, credential-looking, has a component over 40 characters, or is a symlink, path is null and path_withheld carries the vocabulary reason.
free_strings.why_safe: names of items the user owns, read by lstat only, at most two components below the home (database paths are Hermes's own store files); credential-named items are never shown. Serializer: _serialize_dict takes the location from 'path' and EvidenceSerializer.scalar returns the resolved path, which equals the emitted value because it is already resolved; kept unchanged (verified by test). The item must exist at serialization time.

free_strings.what: each finding's affected_identities: the resolved absolute profile directory (empty for not_measured, where the root may not exist)
free_strings.why_safe: house convention for findings (the audited root itself). Serializer: kept unchanged as an existing resolved path (verified by test).

notes: ENVELOPE: audit_home_workdirs returns exactly {home_workdirs, findings, status, coverage, run_metrics}. adapt_component_result keeps every top-level key it does not know (contract.py:615-617), so run_metrics and home_workdirs survive adaptation unchanged; status ('pass') is read only into legacy_status_ignored; coverage is honoured. component_dto (persistence.py:210) keeps only component_id/coverage/classification/findings, so the caller must take res['run_metrics'] from the adapted result and store it outside the fingerprinted report, and take res['home_workdirs'] into finalize_run(measurements=...) like write_settings.

WIRING: in audit_surface._sweep under full_home: _component('home_workdirs', identity, home_workdirs.audit_home_workdirs, profile_path=profile['path']); add 'home_workdirs' to the measurements dict and to store.finalize_run's section loop (store.py:1144). The key 'home_workdirs' itself is listed in schema_keys because it is the report key.

SEALING SETS: add schema_keys to evidence_vocabulary.SCHEMA_KEYS; vocabulary to evidence_vocabulary.VOCABULARY; rule_ids to evidence_constants.RULE_IDS; consequences to evidence_constants.FINDING_CONSEQUENCES (ALLOWED_FINDING_CONSEQUENCES and evidence.CODE_LABELS follow from it); numeric_evidence_keys to persistence._EVIDENCE_NUMERIC_KEYS; vocab_evidence_keys to persistence._EVIDENCE_VOCAB_KEYS. Rule ids and consequence sentences must also be VOCABULARY members (evidence.VOCABULARY already unions RULE_IDS and CODE_LABELS).

FREE STRINGS: the section and findings emit no string the serializer would tokenise. Names are emitted only as absolute paths of existing items under the resolved home (key path), or withheld with a vocabulary reason in path_withheld (undecodable_name, credential_named, long_name, symlink); not_hermes_folders[].name and the relative_path fields were removed. not_measured findings carry no identity or path (a missing root would be tokenised). Tests: two runs sealed with separate serializers are identical, and no dict with an hmac field appears in any sealed output. Paths must still exist when the report is sealed.

DIGEST: the section and findings hold no clock-derived value (only run_metrics.elapsed_ms). Exception inherent to the cap: when max_seconds cuts the walk, the partial numbers depend on run speed; such a section always has coverage could_not_verify and truncated_by max_seconds.

REACHABILITY: truncated_by 'lstat_error' needs an entry that vanishes between scandir and lstat (tests simulate it with a wrapped os.scandir). 'io_error' is a defensive fallback in the could_not_verify finding's evidence and is unreachable in the current code (every cut sets truncated_by); it is listed so the vocabulary stays closed if that changes.

PER-RUN FIELD OUTSIDE THIS MODULE: finding_dto adds evidence.source_digest = digest(finding), keyed with the run's serializer key (persistence.py:110-113,177); it is a hex string, not an hmac token, but it varies between runs for every section's findings. Known limit: this module does not change it.

SYMLINKS: symlinks are never followed; each counts in symlinks_skipped; a top-level symlink is listed in not_hermes_folders with kind symlink, size 0 and path withheld (symlink); file sizes are st_size, not unique disk blocks, so totals over shared-block or hard-linked files are an upper bound.
COMPONENT ID: 'home_workdirs' is in vocabulary because the store seals the adapted component envelope (component_id) through serialize_evidence (store.py:427-436); it would otherwise become a token.
